claims.text: Critic-driven decoding combines the probabilistic output of a generator language model with the output of a binary text critic classifier that evaluates the match between input data and the generated prefix.
Training the text critic classifier does not require additional datasets beyond the base language model's training data and synthesized negative examples.
On the WebNLG benchmark, critic-driven decoding using the base critic achieves an NLI score of 0.855 compared to 0.841 for the baseline.
On the WebNLG benchmark, critic-driven decoding using the base critic increases BLEURT score from 0.128 (baseline) to 0.155.
In human evaluation on WebNLG outputs, the base critic reduces the rate of major hallucinations from 0.40 (baseline) to 0.30.
On the OpenDialKG benchmark, the base critic decoding approach improves the NLI score from 0.748 (baseline) to 0.796.
On the OpenDialKG benchmark, the base critic decoding approach improves the BLEURT score from -0.933 (baseline) to -0.905.
Critics trained on negative examples generated by the fine-tuned language model fail to improve the NLI score on WebNLG over the baseline.

evidence.description: The authors define critic-driven decoding via Eq. 3 and 4, combining standard conditional LM probability with a critic probability P(c|y<=i, x) conditioned on the current token prefix and input data.
Positive instances are constructed from prefixes of (x,y) pairs in the base LM dataset, and negative instances are synthesized using base text modifications, LM sampling, or reference replacing.
Table 2 reports an overall WebNLG NLI score of 0.855 for '1. critic (base)' compared to 0.841 for the baseline.
Table 2 reports an overall WebNLG BLEURT score of 0.155 for '1. critic (base)' compared to 0.128 for the baseline.
Table 5 reports major hallucination frequency of 0.30 for '1. critic (base)' compared to 0.40 for the baseline.
Table 3 shows OpenDialKG NLI metric of 0.796 for '1. critic (base)' versus 0.748 for standard decoding baseline.
Table 3 shows OpenDialKG BLEURT metric of -0.905 for '1. critic (base)' versus -0.933 for standard decoding baseline.
Table 2 reports NLI scores of 0.834 (fine-tuned LM) and 0.839 (fine-tuned LM w. full sentences) compared to 0.841 for baseline.

methodologies.name: Critic-Driven Decoding
methodologies.description: A decoding technique that adjusts next-token probabilities from a generator LM by combining them with confidence scores from a binary prefix-coherence classifier.
conditions: Evaluated on top k=5 candidates per step
Linear warmup of critic weight lambda over the first 5 tokens

limitations.text: Existing hallucination mitigation approaches typically require modifying model architecture or acquiring additional training data.
Standard text classifier usage in generation involves generating many outputs with a base model and reranking afterwards.
A certain proportion of hallucinations still remains in the NLG output across all evaluated setups.
The performance of the approach is constrained by the base language model and its top candidate next tokens.
Evaluating the critic classifier at decoding steps slows down the decoding process.
The critic model may become less effective when applied to datasets with noisy training data.
